name: Power Bank (Portable Charger)
shortAnswer: Yes, you can bring power banks in your carry-on bag up to 100 Wh, but they are strictly prohibited in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: The TSA and FAA allow lithium-ion power banks and portable chargers in carry-on bags only. Because lithium batteries carry a fire risk in the cargo hold, they are never allowed in checked luggage. Standard power banks rated at 100 watt-hours (Wh) or less—roughly 27,000 mAh at 3.7V—are permitted in your cabin bag without airline approval. If your portable charger is between 101 Wh and 160 Wh, you must get explicit approval from your airline before flying, and you are limited to two spare batteries. Any power bank exceeding 160 Wh is completely banned on passenger aircraft.
packingTip: Keep your power bank in an easy-to-reach outer pocket of your backpack or personal item so you can grab it quickly if security asks to inspect it. Make sure the capacity label in Wh or mAh is clearly visible, and use a small pouch to prevent the charging ports from short-circuiting against keys or coins.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved power bank 20000mah

faqs.question: Can I put a power bank in my checked luggage?
faqs.answer: No. All spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks must be packed in your carry-on bag due to fire safety regulations.

faqs.question: What is the maximum mAh allowed for a power bank on a plane?
faqs.answer: Most standard power banks up to 27,000 mAh (100 Wh) are allowed in carry-on luggage without special airline approval.

faqs.question: How many power banks can I bring in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: TSA does not set a strict limit on power banks under 100 Wh for personal use, though airlines typically allow up to two larger batteries between 101 Wh and 160 Wh.

name: Laptop
shortAnswer: Yes, laptops are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage, though TSA and airlines strongly recommend keeping them in your carry-on.
tsaRuleDetail: Laptops are permitted in both carry-on and checked bags on domestic and international flights. Most laptop batteries fall well under the 100 watt-hour (Wh) FAA limit for lithium-ion batteries installed inside devices. At standard airport security checkpoints, you will usually need to remove your laptop from its bag and place it flat in a separate screening bin with nothing on top or underneath it, unless you have TSA PreCheck or are passing through a lane with newer 3D CT scanners. While checked bags are allowed, airlines do not cover electronics for damage or theft in checked luggage.
packingTip: Slide your laptop into a padded sleeve inside a dedicated quick-access backpack compartment so you can pull it out in seconds at the security line. Make sure your laptop has enough battery charge to power on, as TSA officers can occasionally ask you to turn on electronic devices during screening.
amazonKeyword: tsa friendly laptop backpack padded sleeve

faqs.question: Do I have to take my laptop out of my bag at TSA?
faqs.answer: In standard screening lanes, yes, laptops must be placed in a separate bin. If you have TSA PreCheck or use a lane with 3D CT scanners, you can usually leave it inside.

faqs.question: Can I bring two laptops in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes. TSA does not limit the number of personal laptops you can bring, though each one may need its own bin during screening.

faqs.question: Should I put my laptop in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: It is allowed if completely powered off, but strongly discouraged due to the risk of theft, rough handling, and battery safety rules.

name: Vapes & E-Cigarettes
shortAnswer: Yes, vapes and e-cigarettes are allowed in carry-on bags only, and are strictly prohibited in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: Because vapes, e-cigarettes, vaporizers, and disposable vape pens contain lithium-ion batteries and heating elements, FAA and TSA regulations ban them completely from checked baggage. You must carry all vaping devices on your person or inside your carry-on bag so crew members can respond quickly if a battery overheats. Any liquid e-juice bottles or refillable pods must follow the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule, meaning each container must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Charging or using a vape anywhere inside an aircraft is strictly illegal under federal law.
packingTip: Disconnect the tank or pod from the battery before boarding and turn the device completely off to prevent accidental activation and pressure-induced e-liquid leaks during the flight. Store your vape inside a small hard-shell zippered case with a paper towel wrapped around the pod.
amazonKeyword: smell proof vape travel case hard shell

faqs.question: Can I bring a disposable vape in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes. Disposable vapes must be packed in your carry-on bag or pocket and are never allowed in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Do vape pods count as liquids at TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, e-liquid bottles and pre-filled pods count toward your 3-1-1 liquids limit, though small pods easily fit inside your quart-sized bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring THC or cannabis vapes on a plane?
faqs.answer: No. Marijuana and most THC products remain illegal under federal law, even when flying between states where cannabis is legal.

name: Hair Dryer (Blow Dryer)
shortAnswer: Yes, standard plug-in hair dryers and travel blow dryers are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage with no size restrictions.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA permits standard corded hair dryers, travel blow dryers, blow-dry brushes, and diffusers in both carry-on and checked bags on domestic and international flights. Because plug-in hair dryers do not contain lithium batteries or fuel cartridges, there are no special watt-hour or size restrictions beyond your airline's standard carry-on dimensions. Unlike laptops, you generally do not need to remove a hair dryer from your carry-on bag at airport security checkpoints. If you own a rare cordless battery-powered blow dryer, its lithium-ion battery must stay under 100 Wh and remain inside your carry-on luggage.
packingTip: Choose a lightweight folding dual-voltage travel hair dryer if you fly internationally, because standard US 120V blow dryers can overheat or blow fuses when plugged into European 220V outlets. Wrap the power cord loosely with a silicone tie and tuck the nozzle inside a soft cloth pouch.
amazonKeyword: dual voltage travel hair dryer folding

faqs.question: Do I need to take my hair dryer out of my bag at security?
faqs.answer: Usually no. Unlike laptops, hair dryers can stay inside your carry-on bag during X-ray screening unless a TSA officer asks for a closer look.

faqs.question: Can I bring a Dyson Supersonic or Airwrap in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, corded Dyson hair dryers, Airwraps, and blow-dry brushes are completely allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage.

faqs.question: Are diffuser attachments allowed on airplanes?
faqs.answer: Yes, plastic and silicone hair dryer diffusers and concentrator nozzles are permitted in both carry-on and checked bags.

name: Electric Toothbrush
shortAnswer: Yes, electric toothbrushes are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, though rechargeable lithium-ion models are safest in carry-on.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA permits electric toothbrushes, sonic brushes, and spare brush heads in both carry-on and checked luggage on all flights. If your toothbrush uses standard alkaline AA or AAA batteries, you can pack it in either bag without concern. If it has a built-in rechargeable lithium-ion battery (like most Oral-B or Philips Sonicare models), FAA safety guidelines allow it in checked luggage only if it is completely powered off and protected against accidental activation. However, keeping rechargeable toothbrushes in your carry-on bag is strongly recommended to avoid battery issues and baggage damage.
packingTip: Always pack your electric toothbrush in a rigid travel case or engage its built-in travel lock so the power button cannot be pressed accidentally inside your luggage. A vibrating suitcase can trigger a manual bag inspection by TSA officers and drain your battery before you arrive.
amazonKeyword: electric toothbrush travel case hard shell

faqs.question: Do I need to take my electric toothbrush out of my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No, electric toothbrushes can stay inside your toiletry bag during X-ray screening.

faqs.question: Can I bring replacement toothbrush heads on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes, replacement brush heads are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags.

faqs.question: Can I pack a water flosser in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the water reservoir is completely empty before you go through airport security.

name: Shampoo
shortAnswer: Yes, liquid shampoo is allowed in carry-on bags in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, and full-size bottles are allowed in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: Liquid and gel shampoos fall under the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule for carry-on luggage. Each container must hold 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) or less, regardless of how much product is left inside the bottle. All of your travel-sized liquids, gels, and aerosols must fit comfortably inside a single quart-sized clear, zip-top plastic bag, with one bag allowed per passenger. If you want to bring full-size shampoo bottles larger than 3.4 oz (100 ml), you must pack them in your checked baggage. Solid shampoo bars are not considered liquids and have no size restrictions in either bag.
packingTip: Transfer your favorite shampoo into leak-proof silicone travel bottles rated at 3 oz (89 ml) to stay safely under the TSA limit. Before screwing the cap on, place a small square of plastic wrap over the bottle opening to prevent leaks caused by cabin pressure changes during the flight.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved silicone travel bottles 3oz

faqs.question: Can I bring a half-empty 8 oz shampoo bottle in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. TSA measures the total capacity of the container, not the amount of liquid left inside. The bottle itself must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller.

faqs.question: Does solid shampoo bar count as a liquid for TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Solid shampoo bars are exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule and can be packed freely in your carry-on bag.

faqs.question: Can I pack full-size shampoo in checked baggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, full-size shampoo bottles are allowed in checked luggage with no 3.4 oz restriction.

name: Razors (Disposable & Safety)
shortAnswer: Disposable and cartridge razors are allowed in carry-on bags, while loose safety razor blades and straight razors must go in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA rules for manual razors depend on whether the blade is fixed or removable. Standard disposable razors and cartridge razors (like Gillette, Schick, or Billie) where the blades are sealed inside plastic cartridges are completely allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, along with extra sealed replacement cartridges. However, double-edge safety razor blades and straight razors with exposed or removable metal blades are strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage and must be packed in checked bags. You may bring an empty safety razor handle in your carry-on as long as the blade is removed before screening.
packingTip: Always snap a plastic blade guard or hard travel cover over your disposable or cartridge razor so you do not accidentally cut yourself when reaching into your toiletry bag. If you pack loose safety razor blades in your checked luggage, seal them in a hard tin or blade bank to protect baggage handlers.
amazonKeyword: travel razor case protective cover

faqs.question: Can I bring a disposable razor in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes. Disposable razors and sealed replacement cartridges are completely allowed in carry-on luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring a safety razor without the blade in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, an empty safety razor handle is allowed in your carry-on, but the removable metal blades must be packed in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Are straight razors allowed in checked baggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, straight razors and loose razor blades are allowed in checked luggage as long as they are safely sheathed or wrapped.

name: Perfume & Cologne
shortAnswer: Yes, perfume and cologne bottles of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less are allowed in carry-on bags, while larger bottles must be packed in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: Perfume and cologne are classified as liquids under the TSA 3-1-1 rule. Many standard retail fragrance bottles are sold in 3.4 oz (100 ml) or 1.7 oz (50 ml) sizes, which means they are allowed in your carry-on as long as they fit comfortably inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Larger bottles (such as 4.2 oz / 125 ml or 6.7 oz / 200 ml) must go in your checked luggage. Under FAA hazardous materials rules for checked bags, medicinal and toiletry aerosols or alcohol-based perfumes are limited to 18 oz (500 ml) per container and 68 oz (2 liters) total per passenger.
packingTip: Instead of risking a broken glass designer bottle in your luggage, pump a few days' worth of your fragrance into a compact 5 ml refillable travel atomizer that takes up almost zero space in your liquids bag and slips easily into a protective pouch.
amazonKeyword: refillable travel perfume atomizer 5ml

faqs.question: Can I bring a 100 ml perfume bottle in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes. 100 ml is equal to 3.4 oz, which is the exact maximum container size allowed in carry-on luggage.

faqs.question: Does solid perfume count as a liquid for TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Solid perfume balms and sticks are generally exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids limit.

faqs.question: Can I bring duty-free perfume larger than 100 ml on a connecting flight?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is sealed in an official tamper-evident bag (STEB) with the receipt visible inside and purchased within the last 48 hours.

name: Deodorant (Solid, Gel & Spray)
shortAnswer: Solid stick deodorant is allowed in carry-on bags with no size limit, while gel, roll-on, and aerosol spray deodorants must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA treats deodorant differently depending on its formula and consistency. Standard solid stick deodorants, powder sticks, and mineral crystal deodorants are not liquids and can be packed in your carry-on bag in any size without taking up space in your quart-sized liquids bag. However, gel, cream, liquid roll-on, and aerosol spray antiperspirants are all subject to the 3-1-1 rule—they must be in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller for carry-on. Full-size aerosol sprays and gels up to 18 oz (500 ml) are permitted in checked luggage as long as spray nozzles have protective caps.
packingTip: Switch to a solid stick deodorant whenever you travel carry-on only so you save valuable room inside your quart-sized clear liquids bag for essential items like sunscreen, contact lens solution, toothpaste, or perfume. Keep the cap snapped tight to prevent smudges.
amazonKeyword: travel size solid deodorant tsa approved

faqs.question: Does stick deodorant have to go in my liquids bag?
faqs.answer: No. Solid stick deodorant is exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule and can stay in your regular toiletry pouch.

faqs.question: Can I bring aerosol spray deodorant in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the can is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits inside your quart-sized clear liquids bag.

faqs.question: Is gel deodorant considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clear gel and liquid roll-on deodorants count as liquids and must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less in carry-on bags.

name: Sunscreen
shortAnswer: Liquid, lotion, and spray sunscreens must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less in carry-on bags, while solid sunscreen sticks and full-size checked bottles are allowed.
tsaRuleDetail: Sunscreen lotions, creams, oils, gels, and aerosol sprays all fall under the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule for carry-on luggage. Every bottle, tube, or spray can in your carry-on must be labeled 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fit comfortably inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Remember that TSA measures the printed bottle size, not how much lotion remains inside. Solid wax-based sunscreen sticks and dry mineral powder sunscreens are not classified as liquids and have no size restriction in carry-on bags. Full-size sunscreen bottles and capped aerosol cans are allowed in checked baggage.
packingTip: Pack a solid facial sunscreen stick in your carry-on for quick reapplication and save your 3.4 oz liquid slots for body lotion—or buy a full-size bottle after you land if you are flying carry-on only for a week-long beach vacation.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved travel size sunscreen 3oz

faqs.question: Does sunscreen stick count as a liquid for TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Solid wax-based sunscreen sticks are not considered liquids and can be packed freely in your carry-on.

faqs.question: Can I bring spray sunscreen in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, full-size aerosol sunscreen cans are allowed in checked luggage as long as they have a cap protecting the nozzle.

faqs.question: Is aloe vera gel allowed in carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, but aloe vera gel is treated as a liquid and must be in a container of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less.

name: Toothpaste
shortAnswer: Yes, toothpaste is allowed in carry-on bags in tubes of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, and full-size tubes are allowed in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: Because toothpaste is a squeezable paste or gel, TSA strictly enforces the 3-1-1 liquids rule on all carry-on tubes. Your toothpaste tube must be labeled 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Even if a regular 5 oz or 6 oz family-size tube is almost completely empty, TSA officers can still confiscate it because they judge by the container's printed volume. Full-size tubes are always allowed in checked luggage. If you want to skip the liquid rule altogether, dry toothpaste tablets and tooth powders have no liquid restrictions in carry-on bags.
packingTip: Keep a dedicated 0.85 oz to 3 oz travel-size toothpaste tube permanently packed inside your clear TSA toiletry bag so you never accidentally grab your full-size bathroom tube on travel morning, or switch to chewable toothpaste tablets for zero-mess flights.
amazonKeyword: travel toothpaste tablets tsa approved

faqs.question: Can I bring a regular 4 oz toothpaste tube if it is half empty?
faqs.answer: No. TSA bases the rule on the total volume printed on the tube, not how much toothpaste is left inside.

faqs.question: Do toothpaste tablets count as a liquid?
faqs.answer: No, dry toothpaste tablets are solid and do not need to go inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring mouthwash in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the mouthwash bottle is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

name: Nail Clippers & Tweezers
shortAnswer: Yes, standard nail clippers, nail files, and tweezers are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows standard fingernail clippers, toenail clippers, tweezers, metal cuticle pushers, and glass or metal nail files in both carry-on and checked bags on domestic and international flights. Standard nail clippers that include a tiny fold-out metal nail file are also completely permitted through security checkpoints. However, if your manicure set includes sharp grooming scissors with blades longer than 4 inches (10 cm) from the pivot point, or razor-style callus shavers with exposed removable blades, you must remove those specific pieces and pack them in your checked luggage.
packingTip: Keep your nail clippers, tweezers, cuticle trimmer, and nail file neatly zipped inside a compact hard-shell travel manicure case so small sharp metal tools do not get lost at the bottom of your carry-on bag or poke through fabric pockets.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved travel manicure kit

faqs.question: Are metal nail files allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard metal nail files and glass nail files are permitted in both carry-on and checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring cuticle nippers on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes, cuticle nippers and trimmers are allowed in carry-on bags, though final discretion always rests with the TSA officer.

faqs.question: Can I bring nail polish remover in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Liquid acetone nail polish remover is flammable and restricted; use pre-moistened acetone-free nail polish remover pads instead.

name: Peanut Butter
shortAnswer: Peanut butter is treated as a liquid by TSA, so carry-on containers must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, while full jars must go in checked bags.
tsaRuleDetail: Because peanut butter is a spreadable paste, TSA classifies it under the 3-1-1 liquids, gels, and aerosols rule. This means any jar or squeeze pouch of peanut butter in your carry-on bag must be 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) or smaller and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Standard grocery store jars are over this limit and will be confiscated at security if found in your carry-on. However, you can pack full-size jars of peanut butter in your checked luggage with no size limits. Peanut butter already spread inside a sandwich is generally allowed through security.
packingTip: If you want peanut butter for the flight, buy single-serve squeeze packs rated around 1.15 oz (32 g) so they pass TSA security effortlessly inside your liquids bag. If you are checking a full glass or plastic jar, seal it inside a gallon zip-top bag and wrap it in soft clothing.
amazonKeyword: single serve peanut butter squeeze packs travel

faqs.question: Can I bring a peanut butter sandwich through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes. A prepared sandwich with peanut butter spread inside is considered solid food and is allowed in your carry-on bag.

faqs.question: Why is peanut butter considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: TSA rules state that any item you can pour, pump, squeeze, spread, smear, spray, or spill must follow the 3.4 oz (100 ml) carry-on limit.

faqs.question: Can I bring powdered peanut butter in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, powdered peanut butter is allowed, though powder containers larger than 12 oz (350 ml) must be placed in a separate bin for additional screening.

name: Alcohol & Mini Liquor Bottles
shortAnswer: Mini bottles of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less are allowed in carry-on bags, while full-size bottles (under 70% ABV) must go in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows miniature alcohol bottles (typically 50 ml / 1.7 oz) in your carry-on bag as long as they fit comfortably inside your single quart-sized liquids bag and are under 70% alcohol by volume (140 proof). However, FAA regulations strictly prohibit drinking your own alcohol on board an airplane—only alcohol served by a flight attendant may be consumed in flight. In checked luggage, unopened retail bottles under 24% ABV (like wine and beer) have no quantity limit, while spirits between 24% and 70% ABV are limited to 5 liters (1.3 gallons) per passenger. Alcohol over 70% ABV (140 proof), such as Everclear, is banned in both bags.
packingTip: When packing liquor bottles in checked luggage, slide each glass bottle into an inflatable or padded leak-proof bottle protector sleeve and place it in the center of your suitcase surrounded by soft clothing so a rough baggage drop never ruins your wardrobe.
amazonKeyword: wine bottle travel protector sleeves checked luggage

faqs.question: Can I drink mini liquor bottles I brought through TSA on the plane?
faqs.answer: No. Federal law prohibits passengers from consuming personal alcohol aboard a commercial aircraft unless served by flight crew.

faqs.question: How much hard liquor can I put in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Unopened retail bottles of spirits between 24% and 70% ABV are limited to 5 liters (1.3 gallons) per passenger in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring duty-free alcohol in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, full-size duty-free bottles are allowed in carry-on if purchased after security and sealed in a tamper-evident bag with the receipt inside.

name: Reusable Water Bottle
shortAnswer: Yes, empty reusable water bottles are allowed in carry-on bags, while full water bottles are prohibited through security.
tsaRuleDetail: You can bring any empty reusable water bottle—plastic, glass, or insulated stainless steel (such as Hydro Flask, Yeti, or Stanley)—through airport security in your carry-on bag. Once you pass the TSA checkpoint, you can fill it up for free at airport hydration stations. Full water bottles or any bottle containing more than 3.4 oz (100 ml) of liquid will be stopped at security. One helpful exception: completely frozen solid ice inside a water bottle is allowed through TSA as long as there is no melted liquid at the bottom.
packingTip: Empty your bottle before joining the security line and clip it to your backpack or store it in an outer side pocket so you can refill it at the fountain right after screening and avoid paying inflated airport bottled-water prices.
amazonKeyword: collapsible travel water bottle leak proof

faqs.question: Can I bring an empty Stanley cup or Hydro Flask through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Insulated metal tumblers and bottles of any size are allowed in your carry-on as long as they are completely empty.

faqs.question: Can I bring ice in my water bottle through airport security?
faqs.answer: Yes, frozen solid ice is permitted through TSA, but if it has partially melted into liquid at the checkpoint, it must be poured out.

faqs.question: Can I bring a sealed plastic water bottle through TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Even factory-sealed water bottles over 3.4 oz (100 ml) are not allowed through airport security checkpoints.

name: Protein Powder
shortAnswer: Yes, protein powder is allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, though carry-on containers over 12 oz (350 ml) require extra screening.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows protein powder, pre-workout, collagen, and other dietary powders in both carry-on and checked luggage. However, under TSA's powder-screening rule, any powder-like substance in a carry-on container larger than 12 oz (350 ml)—roughly the size of a standard soda can—must be removed from your bag and placed in a separate bin for additional X-ray or swab screening. If officers cannot clear the powder during inspection, they may require it to be placed in checked luggage. Ready-to-drink liquid protein shakes over 3.4 oz are not allowed in carry-on bags.
packingTip: Portion out the exact number of scoops you need into clearly labeled single-serve travel funnels or keep small amounts under 12 oz in their original labeled packaging so TSA agents can identify the powder quickly without delaying your trip.
amazonKeyword: protein powder travel funnel container

faqs.question: Can I bring a full tub of protein powder in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: It is allowed, but tubs over 12 oz (350 ml) will trigger extra screening and take up a lot of space—TSA recommends packing large tubs in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I put protein powder in a Ziploc bag for a flight?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is permitted, though unlabeled white powders in plastic bags are much more likely to be pulled aside for swab testing.

faqs.question: Are creatine and pre-workout powders allowed through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, they follow the exact same 12 oz (350 ml) carry-on powder rule as protein powder.

name: Solid Food & Snacks
shortAnswer: Yes, solid foods like sandwiches, chips, fruit, candy, and baked goods are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags.
tsaRuleDetail: Solid food items are completely permitted through TSA checkpoints on domestic flights. You can bring sandwiches, pizza, burritos, cookies, protein bars, chips, nuts, fresh fruit, and dry cereal in your carry-on bag with no size limit. However, any food that is liquid, creamy, or spreadable—such as soup, yogurt, salsa, hummus, gravy, or jam—must follow the 3.4 oz (100 ml) liquids rule. If you are flying internationally, remember that customs agencies strictly restrict bringing fresh fruits, vegetables, and meats across borders.
packingTip: Pack your snacks in a single easy-to-pull-out pouch near the top of your carry-on, because dense foods like cheese blocks, sandwiches, or pastries can sometimes look unusual on X-ray scans and prompt a quick visual check by security.
amazonKeyword: bento travel snack container leak proof

faqs.question: Can I bring fast food or a sandwich through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solid takeout food like burgers, sandwiches, and burritos are allowed through security in your carry-on.

faqs.question: Are yogurt and pudding allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Only if the container is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring fresh fruit on an international flight?
faqs.answer: You can usually bring it through TSA to eat on the plane, but you must eat or discard fresh fruit before clearing customs in another country.

name: Prescription Medication
shortAnswer: Yes, prescription pills and medically necessary liquid medications are allowed in carry-on bags, and liquids are exempt from the 3.4 oz limit.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows all prescription and over-the-counter medications in both carry-on and checked luggage, though you should always pack essential medicine in your carry-on in case your checked bag is delayed or lost. Pill medications have no quantity limit for personal travel. Medically necessary liquid, gel, and aerosol medications—including insulin, inhalers, and cough syrup—are allowed in reasonable quantities exceeding 3.4 oz (100 ml). Simply declare larger liquid medications to the TSA officer at the checkpoint for separate screening.
packingTip: Keep prescriptions in their original pharmacy bottles with your name clearly printed on the label, especially for international trips, and use a compact travel pill organizer only as a backup once you arrive at your destination.
amazonKeyword: tsa travel pill organizer waterproof case

faqs.question: Do pills have to be in their original prescription bottles for TSA?
faqs.answer: TSA does not strictly require original bottles on domestic flights, but keeping them in labeled bottles is recommended and often required by state laws or international customs.

faqs.question: Can I bring ice packs to keep insulin cold on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes. Medically necessary gel ice packs and freezer packs are allowed in carry-on bags, even if partially thawed, as long as you declare them at security.

faqs.question: Are syringes and EpiPens allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Yes, unused syringes and EpiPens are allowed when accompanied by injectable medication; declare them to the TSA officer before screening.

name: Contact Lens Solution
shortAnswer: Yes, contact lens solution is considered medically necessary by TSA and is allowed in carry-on bags in sizes over 3.4 oz (100 ml) if declared.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA classifies contact lens solution and saline eye drops as medically necessary liquids. This means you are allowed to bring a full-size bottle larger than 3.4 oz (100 ml) in your carry-on bag without placing it inside your quart-sized 3-1-1 bag. However, you must remove bottles over 3.4 oz from your carry-on and inform the TSA officer at the checkpoint so they can perform a quick vapor or X-ray test. Bottles of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller can simply go inside your standard quart-sized liquids bag with no extra steps.
packingTip: If you want to breeze through security without waiting for extra liquid screening, pack a 2 oz or 3 oz travel-size bottle of contact solution inside your quart-sized bag—it is usually plenty for a week-long trip and saves time.
amazonKeyword: travel size contact lens solution 2oz

faqs.question: Can I bring a 12 oz bottle of contact solution in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as you pull it out of your bag and declare it as a medically necessary liquid to the TSA officer for additional screening.

faqs.question: Do contact lenses in blister packs count as liquids?
faqs.answer: Small daily blister packs contain very little saline and are treated as medical items; keep them together in a pouch for easy inspection.

faqs.question: Are eye drops allowed in carry-on luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, prescription and over-the-counter eye drops are allowed in carry-on bags and are exempt from the 3.4 oz limit when medically necessary.

name: Hand Sanitizer
shortAnswer: Yes, liquid and gel hand sanitizer is allowed in carry-on bags in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, while sanitizing wipes have no limit.
tsaRuleDetail: Liquid, gel, and spray hand sanitizers fall under the standard TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule. Each bottle in your carry-on bag must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. (The temporary 12 oz pandemic exemption is no longer in effect.) Full-size bottles of hand sanitizer are allowed in checked luggage, and individually wrapped or pack-style alcohol hand wipes are not considered liquids and can be packed freely in your carry-on.
packingTip: Clip a 1 oz or 2 oz silicone-sleeved hand sanitizer bottle to the outside of your personal item after clearing security, or pack travel-size disinfecting wipes to clean your airplane tray table, seatbelt buckle, and armrests effortlessly.
amazonKeyword: travel size hand sanitizer spray tsa approved

faqs.question: Can I still bring a 12 oz bottle of hand sanitizer in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. TSA returned hand sanitizer to the standard 3.4 oz (100 ml) carry-on liquid limit.

faqs.question: Do hand sanitizer wipes count as a liquid for TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Wet wipes and disinfecting wipes are exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule and can be packed in any quantity.

faqs.question: Can I pack full-size hand sanitizer in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, full-size bottles are permitted in checked baggage.

name: Baby Formula & Breast Milk
shortAnswer: Yes, baby formula, breast milk, toddler drinks, and baby food pouches are allowed in carry-on bags in reasonable quantities over 3.4 oz (100 ml).
tsaRuleDetail: TSA considers baby formula, breast milk, toddler drinks, and liquid baby food medically necessary items, which makes them completely exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule. You may bring reasonable quantities larger than 3.4 oz (100 ml) in your carry-on bag—even if you are traveling without your baby. Ice packs, freezer packs, and frozen gel packs used to cool breast milk or formula are also allowed in carry-on luggage. At security, remove these items from your bag and let the TSA officer know before screening.
packingTip: Use clear, translucent baby bottles or pouches rather than opaque metal containers when possible, because clear containers can often be screened with TSA bottle scanners without needing to be opened or swabbed during security inspection.
amazonKeyword: insulated breast milk cooler bag travel tsa

faqs.question: Do I have to be traveling with my baby to bring breast milk through TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Parents are allowed to carry pumped breast milk and cooling ice packs through TSA even when flying without their child.

faqs.question: Will TSA open my breast milk or formula bottles?
faqs.answer: Usually no—officers use external scanners whenever possible, though you can always request that they use fresh gloves and alternate screening methods if needed.

faqs.question: Are baby food squeeze pouches allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Yes, baby food pouches and jars are exempt from the 3.4 oz limit in reasonable quantities for your trip.

name: Scissors
shortAnswer: Yes, scissors with blades shorter than 4 inches from the pivot point are allowed in carry-on bags; larger scissors must go in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows metal scissors in carry-on luggage as long as the blades measure less than 4 inches (10 cm) from the pivot point (the screw in the middle) to the tip. This covers most manicure scissors, eyebrow trimmers, embroidery scissors, and kid-safe blunt scissors. Any scissors with blades 4 inches or longer—such as kitchen shears, fabric scissors, or full-size office scissors—must be packed in your checked baggage. Keep in mind that international airport security outside the US often enforces stricter limits (such as 6 cm / 2.3 inches).
packingTip: Measure from the center screw to the tip before leaving home, and if your scissors are close to the 4-inch mark, pack them in checked luggage or leave them behind so you do not lose an expensive pair at the checkpoint.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved folding travel scissors

faqs.question: Can I bring small nail scissors in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, small manicure and cuticle scissors are well under the 4-inch blade limit and are allowed in carry-on bags.

faqs.question: Are sewing or embroidery scissors allowed on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the blades are shorter than 4 inches from the pivot point.

faqs.question: Can I bring hair cutting shears in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Only if the blades are under 4 inches from the pivot point; most professional barber shears are longer and should be packed in checked luggage.

name: Lighters & Matches
shortAnswer: One disposable lighter (like a Bic) or one book of safety matches is allowed in carry-on bags; torch lighters and strike-anywhere matches are banned.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA and FAA rules allow passengers to carry one standard disposable butane lighter (such as a Bic) or one Zippo-style lighter in their carry-on bag or pocket. One book of standard safety matches is also permitted in carry-on luggage only. Fuel-filled lighters are prohibited in checked luggage unless completely empty of fuel or enclosed in a DOT-approved travel case. Torch lighters, blue-flame jet lighters, arc/plasma lighters, lighter fluid, and strike-anywhere matches are strictly banned in both carry-on and checked bags.
packingTip: Keep your single disposable lighter in your carry-on backpack pocket and never pack torch, jet-flame, or electric arc lighters—even expensive collectible ones will be confiscated immediately at airport security checkpoints.
amazonKeyword: dot approved lighter travel case

faqs.question: Can I bring a Bic lighter in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, one standard disposable lighter is allowed in your carry-on bag or on your person.

faqs.question: Are Zippo lighters allowed on airplanes?
faqs.answer: Yes, one Zippo lighter is allowed in your carry-on bag, or in checked luggage only if it contains no fuel or is inside a DOT-approved case.

faqs.question: Can I bring a torch lighter or electric arc lighter on a plane?
faqs.answer: No. Torch, jet-flame, and electric arc lighters are prohibited in both carry-on and checked baggage.

name: Umbrella
shortAnswer: Yes, both compact folding umbrellas and full-size stick umbrellas are allowed in carry-on and checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows standard umbrellas in both carry-on and checked bags on domestic and international flights. Compact foldable travel umbrellas easily fit inside backpacks, purses, or roller suitcases without taking up much space. Larger stick umbrellas and golf umbrellas are also permitted through TSA security checkpoints as long as they do not have sharp, weapon-like pointed metal tips. However, keep in mind that individual airlines may count a long stick umbrella toward your carry-on item limit or require it to fit neatly inside the overhead bin.
packingTip: Choose a compact, windproof travel umbrella that comes with a waterproof zippered sleeve so you can slide it straight into your backpack's outer side pocket after a rainstorm without soaking your clothes, chargers, or laptop.
amazonKeyword: compact windproof travel umbrella with case

faqs.question: Can I bring a full-size umbrella in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, TSA allows full-size umbrellas through security, though you should confirm with your airline that it fits their overhead bin size limits.

faqs.question: Do I need to take my umbrella out of my bag at TSA?
faqs.answer: No, compact umbrellas can remain inside your carry-on bag during X-ray screening.

faqs.question: Are beach umbrellas allowed in carry-on luggage?
faqs.answer: No, large beach umbrellas are too long for cabin storage and must be checked as oversized baggage.

name: Pocket Knife & Multi-Tool
shortAnswer: No, pocket knives, Swiss Army knives, and multi-tools with blades are strictly prohibited in carry-on bags and must be packed in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA prohibits all knives and blades of any size in carry-on luggage—including tiny keychain Swiss Army knives, box cutters, Leatherman multi-tools with blades, and folding pocket knives. The only blades allowed in carry-on are round-bladed butter knives and plastic cutlery. You may pack pocket knives and multi-tools in your checked luggage, provided they are safely sheathed or wrapped to prevent injury to baggage handlers. Bladeless multi-tools with tools under 7 inches long are allowed in carry-on bags.
packingTip: Always double-check your keychain and backpack's small zippered pockets before leaving for the airport—forgetting a tiny pocket knife is one of the top reasons travelers lose prized gear at TSA checkpoints.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved bladeless multi tool keychain

faqs.question: Can I bring a tiny keychain Swiss Army knife in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. Even a 1-inch folding blade is strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage and will be confiscated at security.

faqs.question: Are bladeless multi-tools allowed through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, multi-tools without any knife blade are allowed in carry-on bags as long as the tool is 7 inches or shorter.

faqs.question: Can I pack a kitchen knife or pocket knife in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, knives of any size are allowed in checked baggage when safely sheathed or wrapped.

name: Insulin & Diabetic Supplies
shortAnswer: Yes, insulin, syringes, insulin pumps, and cooling gel packs are allowed in carry-on bags and are exempt from the 3.4 oz liquid limit.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA classifies insulin and all diabetes-related medical supplies as medically necessary items, which means they are completely exempt from the standard 3-1-1 liquids rule. You may bring insulin vials, pens, unused syringes, lancets, blood glucose meters, continuous glucose monitors, and insulin pumps through airport security in your carry-on bag in quantities needed for your trip. Freezer packs and gel ice packs used to keep insulin cool are also permitted, even if partially thawed. Simply inform the TSA officer at the checkpoint before screening begins, and always keep insulin in your carry-on because cargo hold temperatures can freeze and ruin it.
packingTip: Pack all your insulin pens, extra pump supplies, and a copy of your prescription inside an insulated diabetic travel cooler bag so everything stays at a safe temperature. Bring at least double the supplies you expect to need in case of unexpected flight delays or cancellations.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved insulated insulin cooler travel case

faqs.question: Can insulin pumps and CGMs go through airport X-ray machines?
faqs.answer: Most manufacturers advise against putting insulin pumps or CGMs through X-ray or full-body scanners; you can always request a manual pat-down and visual inspection instead.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's note to bring insulin syringes through TSA?
faqs.answer: TSA does not strictly require a doctor's note, but keeping your insulin in its original pharmacy-labeled box makes security screening much faster.

faqs.question: Can I put extra insulin in my checked luggage?
faqs.answer: While TSA allows it, you should never check insulin because extreme cold in the airplane cargo hold can freeze and destroy the medication.

name: Asthma Inhaler
shortAnswer: Yes, asthma inhalers and nebulizers are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage, and they are exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids limit.
tsaRuleDetail: Prescription and over-the-counter asthma inhalers are permitted through TSA checkpoints in your carry-on bag, personal item, or pocket without counting toward your quart-sized liquids bag. Because inhalers are pressurized medicinal aerosols, FAA rules allow you to carry them in reasonable quantities for your trip, and keeping your rescue inhaler within arm's reach during the flight is strongly recommended. Portable nebulizers and liquid breathing treatments are also allowed in carry-on luggage, even if the total liquid exceeds 3.4 oz (100 ml). Just declare extra liquid medication vials to the TSA officer before your bag goes through X-ray screening.
packingTip: Keep your primary rescue inhaler in your jacket pocket or the front zippered pouch of your under-seat backpack so you can grab it immediately mid-flight. Pack a spare inhaler in your main carry-on bag with the pharmacy prescription label attached to the box.
amazonKeyword: hard shell asthma inhaler travel case

faqs.question: Do I need to put my asthma inhaler in my quart-sized liquids bag?
faqs.answer: No. Inhalers are medically necessary devices and do not need to be placed inside your 3-1-1 clear liquids bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring a portable nebulizer on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes, portable nebulizers and their saline or medication vials are allowed in carry-on luggage.

faqs.question: Will an inhaler trigger the airport metal detector?
faqs.answer: The small metal canister can sometimes set off walk-through metal detectors, so place it in your carry-on bag or screening bin.

name: EpiPen & Auto-Injectors
shortAnswer: Yes, EpiPens and epinephrine auto-injectors are allowed in carry-on bags with no liquid restrictions, and you should always keep them with you.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows epinephrine auto-injectors—including EpiPen, Auvi-Q, and generic brands—in carry-on luggage and on your person at all times. Because they are life-saving emergency medications, they are completely exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule and needle restrictions. You are allowed to carry multiple auto-injectors (most doctors recommend carrying at least two) without needing a doctor's note, though keeping the printed pharmacy prescription label on the carrying tube or box helps avoid delays. Always pack EpiPens in your carry-on rather than checked luggage so they remain accessible during the flight and protected from extreme cargo temperatures.
packingTip: Store both of your auto-injectors in a brightly colored insulated medical pouch inside your under-seat personal item so you or a travel companion can locate them in seconds. Check the expiration date and viewing window for clear liquid before heading to the airport.
amazonKeyword: insulated epipen carrying case travel pouch

faqs.question: How many EpiPens can I bring in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: TSA does not set a strict limit on the number of EpiPens you can bring; carrying a standard two-pack or extra spares for long trips is completely fine.

faqs.question: Do I have to declare my EpiPen to TSA officers?
faqs.answer: You can leave it inside your carry-on bag for X-ray screening, though letting the officer know beforehand ensures a smooth inspection.

faqs.question: Can an EpiPen go through the airport X-ray machine?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard airport X-ray scanners will not damage epinephrine auto-injectors, though you may request a visual inspection if you prefer.

name: Vitamins & Supplements
shortAnswer: Yes, pill, capsule, and gummy vitamins are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, while liquid vitamins must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less in carry-on.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA permits solid vitamins, herbal supplements, softgels, and vitamin gummies in both carry-on and checked luggage with no quantity limits for personal use. You do not need to keep daily vitamins in their original bottles for domestic flights—weekly pill organizers and travel pouches are completely fine. However, liquid vitamins, tinctures, and fish oil liquids must follow the 3-1-1 liquids rule (3.4 oz / 100 ml or less) in carry-on bags. Powdered supplements follow TSA's powder rule, meaning containers larger than 12 oz (350 ml) in carry-on luggage will need separate screening.
packingTip: Use a compact, moisture-proof weekly pill organizer to pack only the exact number of vitamins and supplements you need for your trip, saving huge amounts of suitcase space. For international travel, keep supplements in their original labeled bottles to avoid customs questions.
amazonKeyword: compact travel pill organizer waterproof 7 day

faqs.question: Can I bring vitamin gummies in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes. Vitamin gummies are treated as solid food/supplements and are allowed in carry-on bags with no size limit.

faqs.question: Do vitamins have to be in their original bottles for TSA?
faqs.answer: No, TSA allows loose vitamins in pill organizers on domestic US flights, though original bottles are recommended for international travel.

faqs.question: Are fish oil capsules considered liquids by TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Gelcaps and softgels like fish oil or vitamin D capsules do not count toward your 3-1-1 liquids limit.

name: CPAP Machine
shortAnswer: Yes, CPAP machines are allowed in carry-on bags, do not count toward your airline carry-on limit, and should always be carried in the cabin.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA permits CPAP, BiPAP, and APAP machines through all airport security checkpoints. Under US Department of Transportation regulations, a CPAP machine in its own travel case is classified as an assistive medical device and does not count against your airline's carry-on or personal item allowance. At standard TSA checkpoints, you will usually need to remove the main CPAP unit from its carrying case and place it in a separate screening bin (you may place it inside a clear plastic bag to keep it sanitary), while masks and tubing can remain in the case. Always empty the humidifier water chamber before screening.
packingTip: Attach a bright medical equipment luggage tag to your CPAP bag so gate agents immediately recognize it as an exempt medical device. Pack a clear gallon zip-top bag inside the case to slip the machine into before placing it in the airport security bin.
amazonKeyword: cpap medical equipment luggage tag travel bag

faqs.question: Does a CPAP machine count as my personal item or carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. On US flights, a CPAP machine carrying only medical equipment flies free as an exempt medical device in addition to your carry-on and personal item.

faqs.question: Can I bring distilled water for my CPAP through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, medically necessary distilled water over 3.4 oz is allowed in carry-on bags if declared to TSA officers for additional screening.

faqs.question: Should I check my CPAP machine?
faqs.answer: No. Airlines strongly advise carrying CPAP machines in the cabin to prevent damage or loss in checked baggage.

name: Ice Packs & Gel Packs
shortAnswer: Frozen solid ice packs are allowed in carry-on bags, while partially melted or liquid gel packs are only allowed if medically necessary.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA rules for ice packs and gel freezer packs depend on whether they are completely frozen or medically required. Standard ice packs used to keep food or snacks cold must be frozen completely solid when you reach the security checkpoint—if they are partially melted, slushy, or have liquid inside, they will not be allowed through unless they are under 3.4 oz (100 ml). However, medically necessary gel packs used to cool breast milk, baby formula, insulin, or other temperature-sensitive medications are allowed in carry-on bags even if partially thawed; simply declare them to the TSA officer.
packingTip: Freeze your gel packs at the coldest setting overnight and pack them inside a high-quality insulated cooler pouch right before leaving for the airport so they stay rock-solid through the security line.
amazonKeyword: reusable ice packs for travel cooler lunch bag

faqs.question: Can I bring a soft gel ice pack for an injury in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as it is frozen completely solid at the checkpoint, or declared as a medically necessary item to the TSA officer.

faqs.question: Are dry ice packs allowed on an airplane?
faqs.answer: Dry ice is allowed in carry-on or checked bags up to 5.5 pounds (2.5 kg) with airline approval and proper vented packaging.

faqs.question: Can I pack liquid gel ice packs in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, gel ice packs in any state—frozen or thawed—are permitted in checked luggage.

name: Wine Bottles
shortAnswer: No, full-size wine bottles are not allowed in carry-on bags through security, but you can pack unopened wine bottles in checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: Standard 750 ml bottles of wine exceed the TSA 3-1-1 liquids limit and are strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage at airport security checkpoints. However, because wine contains less than 24% alcohol by volume (ABV), TSA places no quantity limit on unopened wine bottles packed in your checked baggage—only your airline's weight limit (typically 50 lbs per bag) and international customs allowances apply. The only way to bring a full-size bottle of wine into the airplane cabin is to purchase it at a duty-free shop after clearing security, sealed inside an official tamper-evident bag with the receipt visible.
packingTip: Always slide each glass wine bottle into a padded, leak-proof inflatable wine sleeve before placing it in the center of your checked suitcase surrounded by soft clothes. Never pack wine bottles directly against the hard outer walls of your luggage.
amazonKeyword: inflatable wine bottle protector bags checked luggage

faqs.question: How many bottles of wine can I pack in my checked suitcase?
faqs.answer: TSA has no bottle limit for wine in checked bags, though most travelers pack 2 to 6 bottles to stay under the 50 lb airline weight limit.

faqs.question: Can I bring a corkscrew or wine opener in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: A basic corkscrew without a foil-cutter blade is allowed in carry-on bags, while wine keys with a small knife blade must go in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring mini 187 ml wine bottles in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. Standard mini wine bottles are 187 ml (6.3 oz), which is still larger than the 3.4 oz (100 ml) TSA carry-on limit.

name: Coffee Beans & Ground Coffee
shortAnswer: Yes, whole coffee beans, ground coffee, and instant coffee pods are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows whole roasted coffee beans, ground coffee, instant coffee packets, and single-serve coffee pods (like K-Cups or Nespresso capsules) in both carry-on and checked bags. Whole coffee beans have no size restrictions in carry-on luggage. Because finely ground coffee and instant coffee are classified as powders, containers larger than 12 oz (350 ml) in your carry-on bag may need to be placed in a separate bin for additional screening. Brewed liquid coffee over 3.4 oz (100 ml) is not permitted through security checkpoints, so finish your cup before entering the screening lane.
packingTip: Keep unopened bags of specialty coffee beans in their original factory-sealed valve packaging so TSA officers can easily identify them on the X-ray and your luggage smells great without spilling grounds.
amazonKeyword: airtight travel coffee bean container bag

faqs.question: Can I bring ground coffee in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, ground coffee is allowed in carry-on bags, though bags larger than 12 oz (350 ml) may undergo extra powder screening.

faqs.question: Are K-Cups and Nespresso pods allowed through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, both K-Cups and Nespresso coffee pods are allowed in carry-on and checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring coffee beans back from another country?
faqs.answer: Yes, roasted coffee beans are generally allowed through US Customs, though green (unroasted) coffee beans may be restricted.

name: Protein Bars & Granola Bars
shortAnswer: Yes, protein bars, granola bars, and energy bars are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags with no quantity limits.
tsaRuleDetail: Because protein bars, granola bars, meal replacement bars, and trail mix are solid foods, TSA permits them freely in both carry-on and checked luggage. You can bring a single bar for a quick flight or an entire unopened box of protein bars in your backpack without violating any liquid or powder restrictions. Keep in mind that dense, foil-wrapped nutrition bars can occasionally look opaque on airport X-ray monitors, so officers may briefly inspect them if you pack a large stack tightly together. Liquid protein shakes over 3.4 oz remain prohibited in carry-on bags.
packingTip: Slip your protein bars into a clear zip-top pouch near the top of your carry-on bag so you can pull them out easily if security asks for a quick look—and grab one mid-flight without digging through your luggage.
amazonKeyword: variety pack protein bars travel snacks

faqs.question: Can I bring a whole box of protein bars in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, TSA has no limit on the number of solid protein bars or granola bars you can pack in your carry-on bag.

faqs.question: Are energy gels for runners allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Yes, running energy gels count as liquids/gels, so each packet must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fit inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

faqs.question: Do protein bars need to be taken out of my bag at TSA?
faqs.answer: Usually no, though some airports ask passengers to remove all food items from carry-on bags for clearer X-ray imaging.

name: Cheese (Hard & Soft)
shortAnswer: Hard cheeses like cheddar and parmesan are allowed in carry-on bags, while creamy or spreadable soft cheeses must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA divides cheese into two categories for carry-on luggage. Solid, hard cheeses—such as cheddar, parmesan, swiss, gouda, mozzarella sticks, and manchego—are treated as solid food and are allowed in your carry-on bag in any quantity. However, creamy, spreadable, or liquid cheeses—including cream cheese, brie, camembert, cottage cheese, ricotta, and cheese dip—fall under the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule and must be in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller. All types of cheese are permitted in checked luggage on domestic flights, though international customs rules may restrict dairy products.
packingTip: Pack hard cheeses in wax paper or vacuum-sealed store packaging inside an insulated snack pouch with a completely frozen solid ice pack so they stay fresh throughout your flight.
amazonKeyword: insulated travel snack cooler pouch small

faqs.question: Can I bring brie or cream cheese in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Only if the container is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits inside your quart-sized liquids bag; larger portions must go in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Are string cheese sticks allowed through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, mozzarella string cheese and Babybel wheels are considered solid cheeses and are completely allowed in carry-on bags.

faqs.question: Can I bring cheese back from Europe to the United States?
faqs.answer: Yes, hard and semi-soft cheeses from Europe are generally allowed through US Customs, but you must always declare all food items upon arrival.

name: Honey & Maple Syrup
shortAnswer: Honey and maple syrup are treated as liquids by TSA, so carry-on containers must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, while full jars must be checked.
tsaRuleDetail: Even though honey is thick and sticky, TSA classifies liquid honey, creamed honey, agave nectar, and maple syrup as liquids under the 3-1-1 rule. Any jar, squeeze bear, or bottle in your carry-on bag must be 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) or smaller and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Standard souvenir jars of local honey or maple syrup exceed this limit and will be confiscated at security if packed in carry-on luggage. Full-size bottles and jars of honey or syrup are completely allowed in checked baggage with no size restrictions.
packingTip: Before packing a glass jar of local honey or maple syrup in your checked suitcase, seal it inside two heavy-duty zip-top bags and wrap it in a thick sweatshirt or padded bottle sleeve to prevent sticky disasters.
amazonKeyword: padded glass jar travel protector sleeve

faqs.question: Can I bring a small 3 oz bottle of maple syrup in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the bottle is labeled 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fits inside your quart-sized clear liquids bag.

faqs.question: Are honey sticks or single-serve honey packets allowed through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, individual honey sticks and small packets are well under 3.4 oz and pass easily inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

faqs.question: Is solid honeycomb considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: Raw honeycomb still contains liquid honey, so TSA officers typically enforce the 3.4 oz carry-on limit; pack large jars of honeycomb in checked luggage.

name: Makeup Remover & Wipes
shortAnswer: Makeup remover wipes are allowed in carry-on bags with no limit, while liquid micellar water and cleansing balms must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA rules for makeup remover depend on the product format. Pre-moistened makeup remover wipes and facial cleansing towelettes are not classified as liquids, so you can pack them freely in your carry-on bag without placing them in your quart-sized bag. However, liquid micellar water, oil-based eye makeup removers, and gel or balm cleansers are all subject to the 3-1-1 liquids rule—containers in your carry-on must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller. Full-size bottles of micellar water and cleansing balms are permitted in checked luggage.
packingTip: Swap heavy liquid micellar water for a slim pack of individually wrapped makeup remover wipes or a reusable microfiber makeup-removing cloth that only needs water—both save major space in your liquids bag.
amazonKeyword: travel makeup remover wipes individually wrapped

faqs.question: Do makeup remover wipes count as a liquid for TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Facial wipes and makeup remover cloths are exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule.

faqs.question: Is a cleansing balm considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, soft cleansing balms are treated as pastes/creams and must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller in carry-on bags.

faqs.question: Can I bring travel-size micellar water in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the bottle is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fits inside your quart-sized clear plastic bag.

name: Mascara & Liquid Makeup
shortAnswer: Yes, mascara, liquid foundation, concealer, and lip gloss are allowed in carry-on bags in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA classifies mascara, liquid eyeliner, liquid foundation, concealer, cream blush, and lip gloss as liquids and gels under the 3-1-1 rule. Almost all standard retail mascara tubes (around 0.3 oz / 9 ml) and foundation bottles (1 oz / 30 ml) are already well below the 3.4 oz (100 ml) limit, making them completely carry-on friendly. Technically, they should all fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic liquids bag. Powder makeup—including pressed powder, powder blush, bronzer, and eyeshadow palettes—is not a liquid and has no carry-on restriction.
packingTip: Keep all your liquid cosmetics like mascara, concealer, and foundation inside a clear, TSA-compliant quart-sized zippered toiletry bag so you never have to unpack your regular makeup pouch at the airport security belt.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved clear quart size makeup bag

faqs.question: Does mascara have to go in my TSA liquids bag?
faqs.answer: Officially yes, mascara is a liquid/gel and should be placed in your quart-sized liquids bag, though its tiny size easily fits alongside other toiletries.

faqs.question: Are eyeshadow palettes and powder foundations allowed in carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dry pressed powders and eyeshadow palettes are not liquids and can stay in your regular makeup bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring setting spray in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the setting spray bottle is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

name: Body Lotion & Face Cream
shortAnswer: Yes, body lotion, hand cream, and facial moisturizers are allowed in carry-on bags in containers of 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less, and full-size in checked bags.
tsaRuleDetail: All liquid lotions, body butters, hand creams, serums, and facial moisturizers fall under the TSA 3-1-1 liquids, gels, and aerosols rule. Every tube, jar, or pump bottle in your carry-on luggage must hold 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less and fit inside your single quart-sized clear plastic bag. Remember that TSA measures the printed capacity of the container, not how much cream is left inside. Full-size lotion bottles and large moisturizer tubs are permitted in checked luggage, while solid lotion bars are exempt from carry-on liquid limits.
packingTip: Decant thick face creams and body lotions into small 1 oz or 2 oz leak-proof travel jars with wide mouths so you can scoop out every bit easily without wasting space in your quart-sized liquids bag.
amazonKeyword: tsa approved leak proof travel cream jars

faqs.question: Can I bring a 3.4 oz bottle of hand lotion on a plane?
faqs.answer: Yes, 3.4 oz (100 ml) is the exact maximum container size allowed inside your quart-sized carry-on liquids bag.

faqs.question: Is solid lotion bar considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: No. Solid lotion bars are not liquids and do not need to go inside your 3-1-1 clear plastic bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring prescription hydrocortisone or eczema cream over 3.4 oz?
faqs.answer: Yes, medically necessary prescription creams over 3.4 oz are allowed in carry-on bags if you declare them to the TSA officer.

name: Dry Shampoo
shortAnswer: Aerosol spray dry shampoo must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less in carry-on bags, while non-aerosol powder dry shampoo has no liquid limit.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA regulates dry shampoo based on whether it is an aerosol spray or a loose powder. Standard aerosol spray cans of dry shampoo fall under the 3-1-1 liquids and aerosols rule, meaning carry-on cans must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fit inside your quart-sized clear bag. Full-size aerosol dry shampoo cans are allowed in checked luggage up to 18 oz (500 ml) per can, provided the spray nozzle is protected by a cap. Non-aerosol dry shampoo powders are exempt from the liquid limit, though containers over 12 oz (350 ml) require extra screening.
packingTip: Choose a travel-size 1.6 oz aerosol dry shampoo can or switch to a non-aerosol powder shaker bottle so you can refresh your hair after a long flight without sacrificing space in your liquids bag.
amazonKeyword: non aerosol travel dry shampoo powder

faqs.question: Can I bring a full-size can of Batiste dry shampoo in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: No. Full-size aerosol dry shampoo cans (typically 6.7 oz) exceed the 3.4 oz carry-on limit and must be packed in checked luggage.

faqs.question: Are aerosol dry shampoos allowed in checked luggage?
faqs.answer: Yes, toiletry aerosols up to 18 oz (500 ml) per container are permitted in checked bags as long as the cap covers the nozzle.

faqs.question: Does powder dry shampoo have to go in my liquids bag?
faqs.answer: No. Non-aerosol dry shampoo powders do not count as liquids and can stay in your regular toiletry pouch.

name: Lip Balm & ChapStick
shortAnswer: Yes, solid stick lip balm like ChapStick is allowed in carry-on bags with no liquid limit, while squeeze-tube lip gloss counts as a liquid.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows all types of lip care products in both carry-on and checked luggage. Standard solid wax lip balms—such as stick ChapStick, Burt's Bees, and solid lipstick—are not considered liquids, so you can keep them right in your pocket, purse, or backpack without placing them in your quart-sized liquids bag. Liquid lip glosses, lip oils, and squeezable gel lip balms (like Vaseline tubes or Aquaphor) are technically classified as liquids/gels, though their tiny container sizes are always well under the 3.4 oz (100 ml) limit.
packingTip: Keep a solid stick lip balm in your jacket pocket or personal item for the flight—airplane cabin air is notoriously dry, and a solid stick lets you reapply mid-flight without digging into your liquids bag.
amazonKeyword: hydrating travel lip balm stick pack

faqs.question: Does ChapStick have to go in my TSA liquids bag?
faqs.answer: No. Solid stick lip balms and lipsticks are exempt from the 3-1-1 liquids rule.

faqs.question: Is Vaseline lip therapy considered a liquid by TSA?
faqs.answer: Petroleum jelly and gel lip balms are technically treated as gels, though tiny 0.25 oz tins or tubes easily fit inside your quart-sized bag.

faqs.question: Can I bring multiple lipsticks in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can bring as many solid lipsticks and lip balms as you want in your carry-on bag.

name: Hair Straightener (Flat Iron)
shortAnswer: Yes, corded hair straighteners are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, while cordless battery models face strict carry-on restrictions.
tsaRuleDetail: Standard plug-in hair straighteners and flat irons are completely allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage on US and international flights with no size restrictions. However, cordless straighteners follow stricter FAA safety rules. Cordless flat irons powered by butane or gas cartridges are only permitted in carry-on bags with a safety cover securely fitted over the heating element, and spare fuel cartridges are banned. Cordless models with lithium-ion batteries (like the Dyson Corrale) must generally go in carry-on bags only if the battery has a removable flight-mode disconnect—many airlines ban non-removable lithium battery straighteners altogether.
packingTip: Slide your flat iron into a heat-resistant silicone travel pouch so you can pack it safely even if you just finished styling your hair before heading to the airport, and check for dual-voltage support before international trips.
amazonKeyword: heat resistant travel pouch for flat iron

faqs.question: Do I need to take my hair straightener out of my bag at TSA?
faqs.answer: No, corded flat irons can stay inside your carry-on bag during X-ray screening unless an officer requests a closer look.

faqs.question: Are cordless hair straighteners allowed on planes?
faqs.answer: Only in carry-on bags if they meet strict FAA safety-lock or removable battery rules; always check your specific airline's policy before flying.

faqs.question: Can I pack a hair straightener in my checked suitcase?
faqs.answer: Yes, corded plug-in hair straighteners are completely allowed in checked luggage.

name: Curling Iron & Curling Wand
shortAnswer: Yes, corded curling irons and wands are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, while cordless butane or battery models have restrictions.
tsaRuleDetail: Plug-in electric curling irons, curling wands, and hot rollers are permitted in both carry-on and checked luggage with no TSA size limits. If you are bringing a cordless curling iron powered by a butane gas cartridge, TSA allows one per passenger in carry-on luggage only if a safety cover is securely fitted over the heating element—spare gas refills are strictly prohibited in both bags. Cordless curling irons with lithium-ion batteries must generally stay in your carry-on bag and require a flight-safe disconnect switch to prevent accidental heating during the flight.
packingTip: Use a velcro cord organizer and a heat-proof neoprene travel sleeve to keep your curling wand tidy and prevent the metal barrel from scratching other items in your carry-on.
amazonKeyword: dual voltage travel curling iron with heat pouch

faqs.question: Can I bring a corded curling wand in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes. Standard plug-in curling irons and wands are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags.

faqs.question: Are butane cordless curling irons allowed on airplanes?
faqs.answer: Yes, in carry-on bags only, provided the heating element has a secure safety cover and you do not bring spare butane cartridges.

faqs.question: Can I bring hot rollers through TSA?
faqs.answer: Yes, electric hot rollers and their clips are permitted in both carry-on and checked luggage.

name: Electric Razor & Beard Trimmer
shortAnswer: Yes, electric razors, foil shavers, and beard trimmers are allowed in both carry-on and checked bags, though rechargeable models are best in carry-on.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows electric shavers, rotary razors, beard trimmers, and nose hair trimmers in both carry-on and checked luggage. Unlike loose double-edge safety razor blades, the enclosed oscillating blades on electric trimmers are permitted through airport security checkpoints without issue. If your electric razor runs on a built-in rechargeable lithium-ion battery, FAA safety guidelines strongly recommend packing it in your carry-on bag—if you do place it in checked luggage, it must be completely powered off and protected against accidental activation.
packingTip: Engage the travel lock feature on your beard trimmer or store it inside a rigid zippered travel case so the power switch cannot accidentally turn on and drain the battery—or vibrate inside your bag at security.
amazonKeyword: hard travel case for electric shaver beard trimmer

faqs.question: Can I bring a Philips OneBlade or beard trimmer in my carry-on?
faqs.answer: Yes, electric trimmers like the Philips OneBlade and their replacement heads are allowed in carry-on luggage.

faqs.question: Do I need to take my electric razor out of my bag at TSA?
faqs.answer: No, electric shavers and trimmers can remain inside your toiletry bag during X-ray screening.

faqs.question: Can I bring clipper oil in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, tiny bottles of electric clipper oil are well under 3.4 oz (100 ml) and can go inside your quart-sized liquids bag.

name: Golf Clubs
shortAnswer: No, golf clubs are strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage and must be packed in checked baggage.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA bans all golf clubs—including drivers, irons, wedges, and putters—from airplane cabins because they can be used as bludgeoning weapons. You must check your golf bag with your airline at the ticket counter. Most major US airlines treat a standard golf bag (containing clubs, balls, and one pair of golf shoes) as a regular checked bag under 50 lbs, waiving oversize fees as long as it stays within weight limits. Golf balls, tees, and gloves are allowed in your carry-on bag, though rangefinders with lithium batteries should always be carried in the cabin.
packingTip: Protect your driver and woods from baggage-handling damage by inserting a telescopic stiff-arm support rod inside a padded soft golf travel bag—or use a hard-shell golf travel case—and remove adjustable club heads if possible.
amazonKeyword: padded golf travel bag with wheels stiff arm

faqs.question: Can I bring a single golf putter in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: No. Even a single golf club of any kind is strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage.

faqs.question: Are golf balls and tees allowed in carry-on bags?
faqs.answer: Yes, golf balls, wooden or plastic tees, and golf gloves are permitted in both carry-on and checked bags.

faqs.question: Should I put my golf rangefinder in my checked golf bag?
faqs.answer: Keep rangefinders with lithium batteries in your carry-on bag to prevent theft, damage, and battery safety issues.

name: Skateboard & Longboard
shortAnswer: TSA allows standard skateboards in carry-on and checked bags, but individual airlines enforce size limits and often require checking longboards.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA permits non-motorized skateboards, penny boards, and longboards through airport security checkpoints in both carry-on and checked luggage. However, passing TSA is only half the rule—your airline has the final say on whether your board fits in the overhead bin. Compact cruiser boards and standard decks strapped to a backpack often qualify as a carry-on item on major US airlines, while longer longboards typically exceed cabin size limits and must be checked. Electric skateboards with large lithium-ion batteries over 160 Wh are banned on passenger flights altogether.
packingTip: Slide your skateboard into a padded skate travel bag or remove the trucks and wheels and pack them inside your checked suitcase so the deck fits flat and avoids damaging other passengers' luggage in the overhead bin.
amazonKeyword: padded skateboard travel bag backpack carry

faqs.question: Can I carry my skateboard onto the plane as a personal item?
faqs.answer: Most airlines count a standard skateboard as your main carry-on bag rather than a personal item, and it must fit in the overhead bin.

faqs.question: Are electric skateboards allowed on airplanes?
faqs.answer: Almost never—most electric skateboards have lithium batteries exceeding the 160 Wh FAA limit and are banned in both carry-on and checked luggage.

faqs.question: Can I bring a skate tool in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard T-shaped skate tools under 7 inches long are allowed in carry-on luggage.

name: Fishing Rod & Tackle
shortAnswer: Yes, compact travel fishing rods are allowed through TSA in carry-on bags, while large hooks, sharp lures, and fillet knives must be checked.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA allows fishing rods and reels in carry-on luggage, provided they fit within your airline's overhead bin dimensions—meaning multi-piece travel rods and telescopic rods are usually fine, while long one-piece rods must be checked. Expensive reels and fragile tackle are best kept in your carry-on if permitted. However, large sharp fishing hooks, multi-hook lures, gaffs, and fillet knives are prohibited in carry-on bags and must be packed in checked luggage. Small, lightweight fly-fishing flies are generally allowed in carry-on bags at the TSA officer's discretion.
packingTip: Pack your multi-piece travel rod inside a crush-proof PVC or hard-sided rod tube that meets airline carry-on length limits, and keep sharp treble-hook lures locked in a hard plastic tackle box inside your checked suitcase.
amazonKeyword: hard travel fishing rod tube case carry on

faqs.question: Can I bring fishing line and reels in my carry-on bag?
faqs.answer: Yes, fishing reels and spools of line are allowed in both carry-on and checked luggage.

faqs.question: Are fishing hooks allowed in carry-on luggage?
faqs.answer: Small, delicate fly-fishing hooks are usually permitted, but standard or large sharp fishing hooks and lures must go in checked bags.

faqs.question: Do airlines charge extra for checking a fishing rod tube?
faqs.answer: Most major US airlines treat one fishing rod tube and tackle box as a single standard checked bag without oversize fees.

name: Hiking & Trekking Poles
shortAnswer: No, hiking poles and trekking poles are prohibited in carry-on luggage and must be packed in checked bags.
tsaRuleDetail: TSA prohibits all hiking poles, trekking poles, and ski poles in carry-on luggage—even collapsible carbon-fiber poles with rubber tips—because they are classified as blunt or pointed objects that could be used as weapons. You must pack your trekking poles inside your checked suitcase or duffel bag. The only exception is a medical walking cane or mobility aid needed by a passenger with a disability or injury, which is always allowed through security and into the cabin. Always place rubber tip protectors over sharp tungsten pole tips before packing them in checked luggage.
packingTip: Collapse your trekking poles to their shortest length, snap rubber covers over the carbide tips, and slide them into a padded pole bag diagonally inside your checked suitcase so they do not puncture your clothing or gear.
